newsitem.title: RUSSIA: No change to Yeltsin operation plans - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: No change to Yeltsin operation plans - spokesman.

text.p: There have been no changes to the proposed schedule for Russian President Boris Yeltsin's planned heart operation, presidential spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Monday.

"The preparation for the president's operation are continuing, there are no changes," Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing. Officials have said that doctors plan to operate on the Russian president in the middle of November.

Yeltsin, 65, had two heart attacks last year and some doctors say he may have had a third one between the two rounds of the Russian presidential election. Yeltsin was elected for a new four-year term on July 3.
He is currently resting in the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow while doctors get him ready for the operation, which will improve the blood supply to his heart.

Aides say the president is still in charge of affairs of state, a view backed on Monday by the communist head of the State Duma lower house of parliament who said Yeltsin was taking decisions and was aware of everything going on in Russia.
